summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a persistent nasopharyngeal mass and new-onset right-sided hearing loss with ear pain, following a clinic visit that revealed a peritonsillar mass concerning for abscess. She also reported new left shoulder pain radiating down the arm. Biopsy of the nasopharyngeal mass showed reactive cells with no clear evidence of malignancy or active infection, though findings remain inconclusive regarding possible lymphoma recurrence. Middle ear effusion was attributed to Eustachian tube compression from the mass, with no signs of infection. Shoulder MRI revealed adhesive capsulitis and rotator cuff tendinosis without evidence of neoplasm or septic joint. The patient remained afebrile and asymptomatic, with stable vital signs, and was discharged home without antibiotic therapy. Follow-up was arranged with ENT for the nasopharyngeal mass and ear effusion, and with her PCP for shoulder management. Chronic conditions including CVID, diabetes, and pain were maintained on baseline regimens.
